text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
--- Denmark's third largest Bank BG Bank hopes to secure 25 percent of the country's business client market through intense marketing campaigns and extra staffing.

--- The recent weeks' mobile telephone price war between telecom companies Tele Danmark and Sonofon has upped sales, but retailers complain that intense sales campaigns are causing earnings to fluctuate.

--- Denmark's Chamber of Commerce says many food retail stores estimate turnovers too low to be allowed to open on Sundays according to rules limiting shops trading on Sundays to 12.7 million crowns per annum sales, outcompeting many small stores.

--- A shortage of organ donors has led 30,000 Danes to volunteer as new donors in the past year alone. Some 173,000 Danes are now listed as donors at Denmark's state hospitals compared to only 138,200 in 1995.

--- Denmark's largest chocolate producer Toms Factories is to set up a subsidiary in Poland, aiming at total sales of luxury chocolates of 500 million crowns within the next two years on the Polish market.
